extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how to prepare, present, and process amendments to U.S. patent applications under 37 CFR 1.121, including rules for specification, claim, drawing, and substitute-specification amendments and handling of non-compliant amendments and examiner's amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model or exhibit admission
rubrics_metrics.description: A model or exhibit will not generally be admitted as part of the record of an application. However, a model or exhibit submitted by the applicant which complies with 37 CFR 1.91 would be made part of the application record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the model or exhibit is merely used for demonstration during an interview, it will not be made part of the record; a full description of what was demonstrated must be of record (see 37 CFR 1.133(b)). Demonstrations/exhibits too large may be viewed by the examiner outside the Office with supervisory approval; witnessing such demonstration must be essential to clarifying issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally one interview after final rejection is permitted, but the intended purpose and content should be presented briefly, preferably in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interview may be granted if the examiner is convinced disposal or clarification for appeal may be accomplished with only nominal further consideration. Interviews merely to restate arguments of record or to discuss new limitations requiring more than nominal reconsideration or new search should be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews preceding amendments after allowance (37 CFR 1.312)
rubrics_metrics.description: After an application is sent to issue, it is technically no longer under the jurisdiction of the primary examiner; detailed consideration of claims prior to filing an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 should not be given by interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for interviews on cases where notice of allowance has been mailed should be granted only with specific approval of the Technology Center Director upon a written showing of extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of making amendments (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in applications are made by filing a paper, in compliance with § 1.52, directing that specified amendments be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All amendments filed on or after July 30, 2003 must comply with revised 37 CFR 1.121 to facilitate electronic image processing; non-compliant amendments will result in a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendments format
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the specification (other than claims, computer listings, and sequence listings) must be made by adding, deleting or replacing a paragraph, by replacing a section, or by a substitute specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must unambiguously identify the paragraph/section to be modified (paragraph number, page and line, or other unambiguous method) and be accompanied by replacement or new paragraph(s); replacement paragraphs must include markings showing all changes; new paragraphs must be presented in clean form without underlining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking conventions for specification changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Text of added subject matter must be shown by underlining; deleted matter must be shown by strike-through, except that double brackets may be used for five or fewer consecutive characters or where strike-through cannot be perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double brackets mean square brackets [ ], not parentheses. If strike-through cannot be perceived, deleted matter must be shown within double brackets (e.g., [[4]]). As an alternative, extra portions of text may be included before and after the deleted text in strike-through and the desired change underlined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement section and substitute specification rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments by replacement section require a reference to the section heading and a replacement section with markings showing changes; substitute specifications require compliance with §§ 1.125(b) and (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute specification must be submitted as a clean version and a marked-up version showing changes relative to previous version, and accompanied by a statement that it contains no new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of previously deleted matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A previously deleted paragraph or section may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment adding the previously deleted paragraph or section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A direction to remove a previously entered amendment will not be permitted; once amended in a first amendment document, the paragraph/section shall not be represented in a subsequent amendment unless amended again or a substitute specification is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment sections must begin on separate sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Each section of an amendment document (e.g., specification amendments, claim amendments, drawing amendments, and remarks) must begin on a separate sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended amendment paper order: (A) cover sheet/table of contents with application info; (B) 'Amendments to the Specification'; (C) 'Amendments to the Claims' with complete claim listing; (D) 'Amendments to the Drawings' discussing changes; (E) remarks section; (F) any drawings attachments ('Replacement Sheet', 'New Sheet', 'Annotated Sheet').

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure consistency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter rule
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure of an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be rewritten when amended
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to a claim must be made by rewriting the entire claim with all changes (additions and deletions) as indicated, except when the claim is being canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each amendment document that includes a change to an existing claim, cancellation, or addition of a new claim must include a complete listing of all claims ever presented, including text of all pending and withdrawn claims; the claim listing will replace all prior versions of the claims in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim status identifiers and listing
rubrics_metrics.description: The status of every claim must be indicated after its claim number by using one of the following identifiers in parentheses: (Original), (Currently amended), (Previously presented), (Canceled), (Withdrawn), (New), and (Not entered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative identifiers (e.g., 'Original Claim', 'Presently amended', 'Canceled without prejudice', 'Previously added', 'New claim', 'Not entered claim') may be accepted if clear. In U.S. national stage applications, specific PCT-origin statuses must be used as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When claim text with markings is required
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims being currently amended must be presented with markings to indicate the changes relative to the immediate prior version; added text underlined, deleted matter strike-through.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: (1) for deletion of five or fewer consecutive characters, double brackets may be used; (2) where strike-through cannot be easily perceived, double brackets must be used. An accompanying clean version is not required and should not be presented. Only 'currently amended' or 'withdrawn' claims will include markings. Claims added by amendment must be indicated 'new' and must not be underlined.

rubrics_metrics.name: When claim text in clean version is required
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of all pending claims not being currently amended shall be presented in clean version, i.e., without any markings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation in clean version of claims with status 'original', 'withdrawn', or 'previously presented' constitutes an assertion they have not changed relative to the immediate prior version (except omission of prior markings). Any claim added by amendment must be indicated as 'new' and presented in clean version without underlining.

rubrics_metrics.name: When claim text must not be presented (canceled/not entered)
rubrics_metrics.description: No claim text shall be presented for any claim in the claim listing with the status of 'canceled' or 'not entered.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation is effected by an instruction to cancel a particular claim number; listing a claim as 'canceled' constitutes an instruction to cancel. Canceled and not-entered claims must be listed by claim number and status only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim numbering and preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims in each amendment paper must be presented in ascending numerical order. Consecutive canceled or not entered claims may be aggregated into one statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A canceled claim can be reinstated only by adding the claim as a 'new' claim with a new claim number. Original numbering must be preserved; remaining claims must not be renumbered. New claims after canceling all prior claims must be numbered consecutively beginning with the number next following the highest numbered claim previously presented in compliance with 37 CFR 1.126.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of acceptable claim listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Example illustrating how to list claims with various status identifiers (e.g., 'Claims 1–5 (canceled)', 'Claim 6 (withdrawn): A process ...', 'Claim 8 (currently amended): A bucket with a greenblue handle.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the status identifiers and formatting rules when preparing the claim listing; example demonstrates aggregation, status labels, and presentation of amended and clean claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable alternative status identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will waive certain provisions and accept alternative status identifiers that are not specifically set forth in 37 CFR 1.121(c) if the amendment otherwise complies and the status is accurate and clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of acceptable alternatives provided (e.g., 'Original Claim', 'Presently amended', 'Canceled without prejudice', 'Previously added', 'New claim', 'Not entered claim'). When accepted the examiner need not correct them and applicant will not be required to submit corrective amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing amendment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes to an application drawing must comply with 37 CFR 1.84 and must be submitted on a replacement sheet of drawings labeled 'Replacement Sheet'; any new sheet labeled 'New Sheet'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement sheet must include all figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet even if only one figure is amended. The figure/figure number must not be labeled 'amended'. A marked-up 'Annotated Sheet' may be included and must be presented in the amendment or remarks section explaining the change. A marked-up copy is required when requested by the examiner. No proposed drawing corrections in red ink; proposed corrections will be non-compliant under 37 CFR 1.121(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of drawing changes and specification consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: An explanation of changes to drawings must be presented in the 'Amendments to the Drawings' or the remarks section; the brief and detailed description of drawings in the specification must be amended if inconsistent with drawing changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawing changes are not approved by the examiner, applicant will be notified in the next Office action and must amend specification accordingly; drawing corrections require replacement/new sheets rather than letters to the draftsman.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendments (37 CFR 1.121(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may make amendments to the specification, including the claims, by examiner's amendment without paragraph/section/claim replacement to expedite prosecution and reduce cycle time; such examiner's amendments need not comply with paragraphs (b)(1), (b)(2), or (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner's amendment should include the reason why the amendment is non-compliant and indicate how it was corrected. Authorization from applicant or attorney/agent is not required for non-substantive corrections (format/typographical). Authorization and appropriate extensions are required if changes are substantive (e.g., cancellation of a claim or change the scope of the claims), and must be given within the time period for reply set in the last Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant amendments — notice and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.121, the Office will notify applicant by a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment (Form PTOL-324) identifying: (1) which section is non-compliant; (2) items required for compliance; and (3) reasons why the section fails to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The type of amendment determines whether applicant will be given time to comply and whether the reply should consist of the corrected section rather than the entire corrected amendment. If the non-compliant amendment would otherwise place the application in condition for allowance, the examiner may enter it and provide an examiner's amendment to correct non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant preliminary amendment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a preliminary amendment is filed after the filing date of the application and is non-compliant, the technical support staff will send a notice setting a time period of 30 days or one month, whichever is later, for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No extensions of time are permitted for reply. Failure to submit a timely reply will result in the application being examined without entry of the preliminary amendment. Applicant's reply is required to include the corrected section of the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract amendment guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the abstract: where amendments are minor, the abstract should be provided as a marked-up version using strike-through and underlining; where substantially rewritten, provide a new (substitute) abstract in clean form accompanied by an instruction for cancellation of the previous version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new abstract must not be underlined. Whether marked-up or new, the abstract must comply with 37 CFR 1.72(b) regarding length and placement on a separate sheet. Avoid marking up the abstract so heavily that its meaning is obscured.
